risk_if_not_implemented: Without Phishing-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), credentials may be phished, replayed, guessed or stolen, allowing unauthorized actors to authenticate as trusted identities. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
compensating_control_1.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
(1) Remote network access; 
(2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
(3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive and/or regulated data.
compensating_control_1.justification: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Phishing-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37.2) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Passkeys
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize passkeys, or equivalent cryptographic key pairing technologies, to authenticate users to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
compensating_control_2.justification: Passkeys (IAC-16) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Phishing-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37.2) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
